We hebben onze manager nodig om dit conf.scenario: Your group cannot resolve a conflict without the manager's involvement. Explain that you need your manager to help bring about a resolution.
We hebben onze manager nodig om dit conf.explanation: We takes plural hebben. Onze manager is the person needed, and nodig completes iets nodig hebben. Manager is a de-word, so use onze. Om dit conflict op te lossen gives the purpose of needing the manager: resolving the conflict. It does not specify that the manager must do every part alone. Oplossen is separable, with te between op and lossen; conflict is a het-word, so use dit.

We hebben een oplossing voor het opslagp.scenario: After investigating a storage problem, your group has identified a solution. Announce that you have found a solution, without claiming that it has already been implemented.

answers.text: Dat weet ik niet zeker.
answers.explanation: Dat refers to the claim and is fronted as the object. Finite weet comes next, before subject ik. Niet zeker weten expresses uncertainty about that claim. The original uses zeker zijn van with split daar ... van; both withhold certainty without saying the claim is false.

answers.text: Ze zijn geduldig.
answers.explanation: Zijn agrees with plural ze; geduldig is a predicate adjective without an agreement ending. In this situation the people are waiting patiently now, so zijn geduldig describes the same behaviour as the idiom geduld oefenen. It does not say they are practising a separate training exercise.

answers.text: We hebben ons budget overschreden.
answers.explanation: The scenario explicitly says the group has spent beyond its budget. Hebben ... overschreden reports passing that limit; zitten boven ons budget describes the resulting financial position. Budget is a singular het-word, so use ons. Overschrijden is inseparable in this sense; its participle is overschreden.

Mag ik even iets vragen?.english: May I ask a quick question?

Mijn trein heeft tien minuten vertraging.english: My train is delayed by ten minutes.

Zij kookt graag voor haar vrienden..scenario: A woman regularly enjoys preparing meals for her friends. Tell someone what she enjoys doing; refer to her as she and her friends as a group.
Zij kookt graag voor haar vrienden..explanation: Kookt is the present verb for singular zij/ze. Graag expresses enjoying the activity, so kookt graag means likes cooking. Voor haar vrienden names the people she cooks for; vrienden is plural. Dutch needs no is before kookt.

answers.text: Zij vindt het leuk om voor haar vrienden te koken.
answers.english: She enjoys cooking for her friends.
answers.explanation: Vindt agrees with zij. Het leuk vinden expresses enjoyment. Om ... te introduces the activity; koken is an infinitive, with voor haar vrienden inside that phrase. This is a different structure for the same enjoyment, not just a pronoun swap.

Ze kookt graag voor haar vrienden..scenario: A woman regularly enjoys preparing meals for her friends. Tell someone what she enjoys doing; refer to her as she and her friends as a group.
Ze kookt graag voor haar vrienden..explanation: Kookt is the present verb for singular zij/ze. Graag expresses enjoying the activity, so kookt graag means likes cooking. Voor haar vrienden names the people she cooks for; vrienden is plural. Dutch needs no is before kookt.

answers.text: Zij vindt het leuk om voor haar vrienden te koken.
answers.english: She enjoys cooking for her friends.
answers.explanation: Vindt agrees with zij. Het leuk vinden expresses enjoyment. Om ... te introduces the activity; koken is an infinitive, with voor haar vrienden inside that phrase. This is a different structure for the same enjoyment, not just a pronoun swap.

Wij plannen onze vakantie..scenario: You and your friends are choosing dates and a destination for a shared holiday. Speaking for the whole group, tell someone what you are doing together.
Wij plannen onze vakantie..explanation: Wij is plural, so the finite verb is plannen. Onze agrees with de vakantie, even though vakantie is singular: the possessive ending follows the thing possessed, not the number of owners. Plannen describes arranging the holiday; van plan zijn op vakantie te gaan describes the intention to go.

answers.text: We zijn onze vakantie aan het plannen.
answers.explanation: Zijn agrees with plural we. Aan het + infinitive highlights the ongoing planning activity. Onze vakantie comes before aan het plannen; the scenario explicitly describes planning in progress.

Ik probeerde een nieuw gerecht..scenario: Yesterday you tried a new dish at a restaurant. Tell a friend what you tried during that visit; it was new to you, without specifying whether you already knew about it.
Ik probeerde een nieuw gerecht..explanation: Probeerde is the simple past of proberen with ik; plural would be probeerden. Een nieuw gerecht has no adjective -e because gerecht is a singular indefinite het-word. Nieuw means new; onbekend would mean unknown or unfamiliar. The object een nieuw gerecht follows the finite verb.

answers.text: Ik heb een nieuw gerecht geprobeerd.
answers.explanation: Heb is the perfect auxiliary for ik. Geprobeerd is the participle, at the end of this clause; trying the dish is the same completed event. Simple past fits recounting the visit; perfect commonly reports the experience.

Ik probeerde een nieuwe soep..scenario: At an earlier meal you tried a new soup. Tell a friend what you tried, referring to yourself in the past.
Ik probeerde een nieuwe soep..explanation: Probeerde is singular simple past. Soep is a de-word, so an adjective before it takes -e even after een: een nieuwe soep. Compare een nieuw gerecht, because gerecht is a het-word.

answers.text: Ik heb een nieuwe soep geprobeerd.
answers.explanation: The perfect reports the same completed trial: heb is finite and geprobeerd is the participle. Nieuwe keeps -e because soep is a de-word.

Ik ben het daarmee eens..scenario: Someone has just expressed an opinion. Say that you share that opinion, referring back to what they said.
Ik ben het daarmee eens..explanation: The expression is het eens zijn met iets. Ben is finite for ik; het is a fixed part of the expression. Daarmee means with that: met becomes mee in this pronominal combination. Daarmee comes before eens in the neutral order.

answers.text: Daar ben ik het mee eens.
answers.explanation: Daar starts the main clause, so finite ben comes before ik. Daar ... mee refers to the opinion and het remains part of het eens zijn.

We overwegen alle opties..scenario: Your group has not chosen a solution yet. Speaking for the group, explain that you are considering every option.
We overwegen alle opties..explanation: We takes plural overwegen, which is also the infinitive form in isolation. Overwegen meaning consider is inseparable: not wegen ... over. Alle opties means all options; with a possessive use al onze opties. Do not add zijn before finite overwegen.

answers.text: We denken na over alle opties.
answers.english: We are considering all the options.
answers.explanation: Nadenken over means thinking carefully about something. Finite nadenken splits: we denken ... na; over alle opties names the topic and can follow na. Inseparable overwegen expresses the same consideration without splitting over from wegen. Neither says a decision has been made.

Dit formulier is snel in te vullen..scenario: This form takes very little time to complete. Tell someone that filling it in can be done quickly.
Dit formulier is snel in te vullen..explanation: Dit refers to singular het formulier. In is ... te + infinitive, the subject is the thing that can be acted on. Invullen is separable, so te comes between in and vullen. Snel describes the time needed; makkelijk would describe ease.

answers.text: Je kunt dit formulier snel invullen.
answers.english: You can fill in this form quickly.
answers.explanation: Je is the generic person completing the form. Kunt is finite; invullen stays together as an infinitive after the modal. Both describe how quickly this particular form can be completed.

Ik ben op de bank gaan zitten..scenario: You have just taken a seat on the sofa. Describe the action of sitting down, rather than only your current seated position.
Ik ben op de bank gaan zitten..explanation: Gaan zitten means taking a seat. The perfect uses zijn and the double infinitive gaan zitten: ben ... gaan zitten, not ben ... gegaan zitten. Ik zit describes being seated now; ik heb gezeten describes a past seated state.

answers.text: Ik ging op de bank zitten.
answers.english: I sat down on the sofa.
answers.explanation: Ging is the simple past of gaan. Zitten stays an infinitive after ging. This can describe the same past action in a narrative, although the perfect is common when reporting what just happened.

Ze gaan in de wachtkamer zitten tot de d.scenario: Several patients take seats in the waiting room and wait for one doctor to call them. Describe what the patients do and when their waiting ends.
Ze gaan in de wachtkamer zitten tot de d.explanation: The first ze means they and takes plural gaan. Gaan zitten means take a seat; in de wachtkamer says where. Tot introduces until. In de dokter ze roept, the subject is singular de dokter, so roept is singular; the second ze means them and is the object.

answers.text: Ze nemen plaats in de wachtkamer tot de dokter ze roept.
answers.english: They take seats in the waiting room until the doctor calls them.
answers.explanation: Plaatsnemen means take a seat and splits as nemen plaats. The same patients, place and waiting endpoint are retained. Nemen is plural for ze; roept still agrees with the single doctor.

Verkoop de oude printer aan hem..scenario: A man wants to buy an old printer that your colleague owns. Tell your colleague directly to sell the old printer to that man, referring to the buyer as him.
Verkoop de oude printer aan hem..explanation: Verkoop is the imperative of inseparable verkopen. The item is the object. Aan introduces the buyer; it is not naar, which would express a destination. In je oude auto, je is possessive your, while in Verkoop je de oude auto? je would be the subject of a question.

answers.text: Verkoop hem de oude printer.
answers.explanation: The recipient is an indirect object without aan, before the item being sold. This keeps the instruction, owner, buyer and item unchanged.

Verkoop je oude auto aan Zoë..scenario: Your friend owns an old car and Zoë wants to buy it. Give your friend a direct instruction to sell their old car to Zoë; address the friend as you.
Verkoop je oude auto aan Zoë..explanation: Verkoop is the imperative of inseparable verkopen. The item is the object. Aan introduces the buyer; it is not naar, which would express a destination. In je oude auto, je is possessive your, while in Verkoop je de oude auto? je would be the subject of a question.

answers.text: Verkoop Zoë je oude auto.
answers.explanation: The recipient is an indirect object without aan, before the item being sold. This keeps the instruction, owner, buyer and item unchanged.

Verkoop je oude auto aan hem..scenario: A man wants to buy your friend's old car. Tell your friend directly to sell their old car to him, addressing the friend as you and referring to the buyer as him.
Verkoop je oude auto aan hem..explanation: Verkoop is the imperative of inseparable verkopen. The item is the object. Aan introduces the buyer; it is not naar, which would express a destination. In je oude auto, je is possessive your, while in Verkoop je de oude auto? je would be the subject of a question.

answers.text: Verkoop hem je oude auto.
answers.explanation: The recipient is an indirect object without aan, before the item being sold. This keeps the instruction, owner, buyer and item unchanged.

answers.text: Ik bereid de agenda voor.
answers.explanation: In this offer, the present expresses the next action you commit to. Bereid is finite for ik; separable voorbereiden splits as bereid ... voor. After zal, voorbereiden stays together as an infinitive. Both offer to prepare the same meeting agenda.

answers.text: We hebben veel dingen besproken.
answers.explanation: Hebben ... besproken is the perfect and reports the same completed discussion. Bespraken is plural simple past; besproken is the participle after finite hebben. Bespreken takes a direct object, so veel dingen needs no over.

answers.text: Ik ben klaar met mijn training.
answers.explanation: Klaar zijn met iets means being finished with it. Ben agrees with ik; met introduces the completed activity. The context says the training is completed. Contrast klaar voor mijn training, which means ready to begin it.

answers.text: Zij heeft de route uitgelegd.
answers.explanation: The perfect uses heeft ... uitgelegd. The particle joins the participle: uit + ge + legd. Legde ... uit is simple past. Both report the same woman's earlier explanation of the route.

answers.text: We kochten het voor haar.
answers.explanation: Kochten is plural simple past of kopen and agrees with we. Het remains the purchased item and voor haar the beneficiary. Hebben ... gekocht and this simple past can both report the completed purchase.

answers.text: Ik bel nu.
answers.english: I'm making a phone call now.
answers.explanation: Bel is finite present for ik. Dutch present can describe an action happening now; nu makes that timing explicit. Ben aan het bellen foregrounds the ongoing activity. Both describe the same current call.

Ik werk vandaag thuis..explanation: Ik takes present werk. Vandaag means today and thuis means at home; the Dutch present can describe today’s ongoing work without an extra ben. With vandaag first, use Vandaag werk ik thuis.

Mijn broer woont in Gent..explanation: The whole subject is mijn broer, singular, so wonen becomes woont. Mijn is possessive my. In Gent names his place of residence; Gent is Ghent in English.

Wij leren elke dag Nederlands..explanation: Wij is plural and takes leren. Elke dag means every day, so this describes a routine. Nederlands names the language and has no article in this expression.

Ik controleer de bestelling..explanation: Controleer is the finite present for ik; do not add ben before it. Controleren means check here, rather than take control of. De bestelling is the order being checked.

De les begint om negen uur..explanation: De les is singular, so beginnen becomes begint. Om negen uur gives the starting time: at nine o’clock. Beginnen is inseparable; the initial be- does not split off.

Mijn collega schreef gisteren een versla.explanation: Schreef is the irregular singular simple past of schrijven; plural is schreven and the participle is geschreven. Mijn collega is singular. Gisteren gives yesterday, and een verslag is the report written.

Ik zocht gisteren mijn sleutels..explanation: Zocht is singular simple past of zoeken; plural is zochten and perfect is heb gezocht. Zoeken takes the thing sought directly: mijn sleutels, without a word corresponding to English for. Searching does not assert that the keys were found.

Hij betaalde met zijn kaart..explanation: Betaalde is singular simple past of betalen, with -de. Met introduces the payment method. Zijn before kaart means his, not the verb be. This says he used his card, without specifying debit versus credit.

De kinderen spelen in de tuin..explanation: De kinderen is a plural subject, so use spelen. In de tuin gives the location. The Dutch present can describe what is happening now: English are playing needs no extra zijn in this model.

Ik begrijp deze uitleg..explanation: Begrijp is first-person present of begrijpen, meaning understand. Uitleg is a de-word, so deze means this before it. This describes understanding the explanation, rather than merely hearing it.

Wij probeerden een nieuw restaurant..explanation: Wij takes plural past probeerden; singular would be probeerde. Restaurant is a het-word, so the adjective after indefinite een is nieuw. Trying a restaurant here means eating there to experience it, not attempting to build one.

Hij werkte gisteren thuis..explanation: Werken has stem werk ending in k, so singular simple past adds -te: werkte. Hij is singular; gisteren means yesterday and thuis means at home. Gisteren does not universally require simple past; Hij heeft gisteren thuis gewerkt is also possible.

Zij belde haar moeder..explanation: Belde is singular simple past of bellen. Zij refers to the woman, and haar moeder is the person she called. Bellen takes this person as a direct object, without a preposition.

Wij woonden vroeger in Gent..explanation: Wonen has stem woon; plural simple past is woon + den = woonden. Wij names the household as a group. Vroeger means in the past or formerly, so the natural English meaning here is used to live.

Ik danste met mijn vrouw..explanation: Dansen has stem dans ending in s, so simple past is danste and the participle is gedanst. Met mijn vrouw identifies the dance partner. Ik is singular; the plural past would be dansten.

De vergadering eindigde om vijf uur..explanation: De vergadering is singular, so use eindigde; plural meetings would eindigden. Om vijf uur gives the ending time. Eindigen has stem eindig and takes -de in the singular past.

Mijn collega controleerde de voorraad..explanation: Mijn collega is one person, so the regular simple past is controleerde. De voorraad means the stock or inventory checked. The present first-person form is controleer; the perfect participle is gecontroleerd.

Ik las gisteren een boek..explanation: Las is singular simple past of lezen; plural is lazen and the participle is gelezen. Gisteren means yesterday. Een boek is what was read; the sentence does not explicitly say every page was finished.

Zij kocht een nieuwe jas..explanation: Kocht is singular simple past of kopen; plural is kochten and the participle is gekocht. Zij means she here. Jas is a de-word, so use een nieuwe jas, with an adjective ending in -e even after een.

We maakten plannen voor het weekend..explanation: Maken has stem maak ending in k, so plural simple past is maakten with -ten. Plannen is a plural noun here, not the verb plannen. Voor het weekend gives the time the plans concern.

Ik heb een nieuw recept geprobeerd..explanation: Heb is finite and agrees with ik; geprobeerd is the regular participle of proberen. Recept is a het-word, so after een use nieuw without -e. The recipe was tried; this does not guarantee a successful result.

Wij hebben de soep geproefd..explanation: Wij takes plural hebben; geproefd is the participle of proeven. The stem proef ends in f, but proeven has v before -en, so the participle ends in -d. De soep is what was tasted, without claiming it was cooked or completely eaten.

Hij heeft de bestelling gecontroleerd..explanation: Hij takes singular heeft; gecontroleerd is the participle of controleren. De bestelling is the object checked, placed before the participle. This reports the completed check without claiming the order contained no errors.

Ik heb mijn kamer opgeruimd..explanation: Opruimen means tidy up, such as putting possessions away. Its participle is op + ge + ruim + d = opgeruimd. Heb agrees with ik; mijn kamer is the room tidied. Tidying does not necessarily mean removing dirt.

Zij heeft de ramen schoongemaakt..explanation: Schoonmaken means clean away dirt. Its participle is schoon + ge + maak + t = schoongemaakt. Zij takes singular heeft here. De ramen is plural windows and comes before the participle.

Wij hebben twee uur gefietst..explanation: This describes cycling as an activity, so its perfect uses hebben. Twee uur measures its duration and needs no voor in this expression. A destination changes the construction: Wij zijn naar huis gefietst describes cycling home.

Ik ben naar huis gefietst..explanation: The destination naar huis makes this directed movement, so the perfect uses zijn: ik ben gefietst. Compare ik heb twee uur gefietst for a cycling activity measured by duration. Naar huis means homeward; thuis instead means at home.

Hij is vroeg vertrokken..explanation: Vertrekken uses zijn for departure: hij is vertrokken. Vroeg means early. The irregular simple past is vertrok (singular), vertrokken (plural); the participle is also vertrokken.

Zij heeft haar moeder gebeld..explanation: Zij is singular she here and takes heeft. Gebeld is the regular participle of bellen. Haar moeder is her mother, the direct object identifying the person called; it is not the subject.

We hebben over het probleem gesproken..explanation: We takes plural hebben; gesproken is the irregular participle of spreken. Over het probleem names the topic. This full prepositional phrase may also follow gesproken, as in the alternate model.

Ik heb het gisteren afgemaakt..explanation: Afmaken forms participle afgemaakt, with ge between af and maak. Heb agrees with ik. Unstressed object het occurs early, before gisteren and afgemaakt; it refers to the task already mentioned.

De trein is op tijd aangekomen..explanation: Aankomen uses zijn in this arrival sense. Aangekomen contains the separable particle aan before ge + komen. De trein is singular, so use is. Op tijd means on time, not merely early.

Ik had de soep al gemaakt..explanation: Had is the past form of auxiliary hebben for ik. With gemaakt it forms the past perfect: the soup was made before the later arrival. Al means already and comes before the participle.

Wij hadden het rapport al gelezen..explanation: Wij takes plural hadden. Gelezen is the irregular participle of lezen. Hadden ... gelezen places the reading before the recalled meeting; al means already. Het rapport is the item read.

Zij had de brief al geschreven..explanation: Zij means she in this situation, so use singular had. Geschreven is the participle of schrijven. Al marks that the letter had already been written before the later request.

Ik had mijn huiswerk al gemaakt..explanation: Had ... gemaakt is past perfect: completion precedes the recalled request. Huiswerk maken means do homework, not manufacture it. Mijn is possessive my; al means already.

Hij was al naar huis gegaan..explanation: Gaan uses zijn for this movement, so its past perfect is was ... gegaan, not had gegaan. Hij is singular. Al naar huis gegaan means he had already gone home before the speaker arrived.

We waren vroeg vertrokken..explanation: We takes plural waren, the past form of zijn. Vertrekken uses zijn for departure, so waren vertrokken is past perfect. Vroeg means early and the departure precedes the later past moment in the story.

Ik had de deur al op slot gedaan..explanation: De deur op slot doen means lock the door. Doen has participle gedaan and uses hebben here; had ... gedaan places the locking before the reminder. Op slot remains a separate phrase rather than joining gedaan.

Zij had het nieuws al gehoord..explanation: Zij refers to one woman and takes had. Gehoord is the participle of horen; had ... gehoord places hearing before the later conversation. Het nieuws means the news and is not a plural noun here.

Wij hadden de rekening al betaald..explanation: Wij takes plural hadden. Betalen forms betaald without extra ge- because of unstressed be-. Hadden ... betaald places paying before the waiter’s later request; al means already.

Ik had de kamer opgeruimd voordat zij kw.explanation: Had ... opgeruimd describes tidying completed before her arrival. Opruimen forms participle opgeruimd. Voordat introduces its own subordinate clause: zij is its subject and kwam, singular past of komen, closes that clause.

De trein was al vertrokken toen ik aankw.explanation: The train’s departure uses past perfect was ... vertrokken because vertrekken takes zijn. Toen introduces the later past event, with its own subject ik and final finite verb aankwam. Aankomen stays joined in that subordinate clause; a main clause would say ik kwam aan.

Hij had het probleem al opgelost..explanation: Had ... opgelost places solving before the later discussion. Oplossen forms participle op + ge + los + t. Hij is the person who solved it, and het probleem is the object. Al means already.

Ik wil de soep proberen..explanation: Wil is finite for ik; proberen remains an infinitive without te directly after wil. De soep is its object. This means trying the soup itself. Compare Ik wil proberen de soep te maken, where proberen introduces a separate te-infinitive.

Wij moeten de deur sluiten..explanation: Wij takes plural moeten; sluiten remains an infinitive after that modal. De deur is the direct object. Moeten expresses the group’s obligation to close it, rather than merely its ability.

Hij kan morgen niet komen..explanation: Kan is singular present of kunnen, and komen remains an infinitive. Morgen supplies tomorrow; niet negates his ability to come. The Dutch present modal can refer to tomorrow without an extra zal.

Ik zal proberen te slapen..explanation: Zal is finite for ik and takes infinitive proberen without te. Proberen itself requires te before slapen. This preserves both relationships: zal proberen, proberen te slapen. The promise concerns trying; it does not guarantee sleep.

We zullen proberen het lek te repareren..explanation: We takes plural zullen. Proberen remains an infinitive after zullen, but introduces its own te-infinitive repareren. Het lek is the object of repareren and comes before te repareren. The group commits to trying rather than guaranteeing success.

Zij mag hier parkeren..explanation: Zij means she here, so mogen becomes singular mag. Parkeren stays an infinitive without te after mag. Hier gives the permitted location. This expresses permission, not a prediction that she will park.

Je moet het morgen afmaken..explanation: Je is the subject and takes moet. Het is the task, placed before morgen and infinitive afmaken. Afmaken stays joined after the modal. This is an obligation to finish tomorrow, not a claim the task is already done.

Wil je deze soep proberen?.explanation: Wil is finite before subject je; proberen remains a bare infinitive. Soep is a de-word, so deze means this before it. This question offers a taste without asserting that the listener wants one.

Mag ik dit gerecht proberen?.explanation: Mag is finite for ik and asks permission. Gerecht is a het-word, so use dit before it; compare deze soep. Proberen remains an infinitive without te after mag.

Moet je het morgen afmaken?.explanation: Moet starts this neutral yes/no question before subject je. Het is the task, morgen the proposed completion day, and afmaken the final infinitive. This asks about obligation; Heb je het al afgemaakt? instead asks about completed work.

Mag ik met de kaart betalen?.explanation: Mag ik asks permission and betalen remains an infinitive. Met de kaart names the payment method. Kaart is a de-word; the context means bank card, without specifying credit versus debit.

Kan ik de jas passen?.explanation: Kan is finite for ik. Passen is an infinitive and means try on the coat in this shopping context. It can mean fit in another construction: De jas past mij means The coat fits me.

Wil je de deur sluiten?.explanation: Wil before je asks about willingness or desire in this scenario; sluiten remains an infinitive. The same wording can serve as a request to close the door in another context, so English Do you want to...? is not its only possible use.

Waar woont je broer?.explanation: Waar asks for location. The subject is the whole phrase je broer, meaning your brother. Je is possessive here, so woont retains its -t; it is not the subject-je inversion pattern woon je.

Wie heeft de deur gesloten?.explanation: Wie is itself the subject who; no additional subject follows heeft. Heeft is the finite auxiliary and gesloten the irregular participle of sluiten. De deur is the object, placed before the participle.

Heb je het al afgemaakt?.explanation: Compare statement je hebt with question heb je: subject je follows the finite auxiliary, so the added -t is omitted. Het is the task, al means already/yet in this question, and afgemaakt is the participle of separable afmaken.

Verkoop je de oude auto aan Zoë?.explanation: Verkoop is finite and je is subject you in this yes/no question. Aan Zoë identifies the buyer. Compare the command Verkoop je oude auto aan Zoë, where je means your before oude auto and no subject is stated.

Probeer dit gerecht eens!.explanation: Probeer is the imperative stem of proberen; no subject is stated. Dit agrees with het gerecht. Eens softens this encouragement, roughly give it a try, rather than requiring exactly one tasting.

Ruim je kamer op..explanation: Opruimen separates in this command: ruim ... op. Je means your before kamer, not subject you. The instruction is to put things away; removing dirt would instead be schoonmaken.

Maak de ramen schoon..explanation: Schoonmaken separates into imperative maak and particle schoon. De ramen is the object, between them. This means cleaning away dirt, not merely putting objects away.

Lees de brief voor..explanation: Voorlezen means read aloud and separates in this command: lees ... voor. De brief is what is read. Voor is the verb’s particle here, not a preposition needing another noun after it.

Geef het boek aan je broer..explanation: Geef is the imperative stem of geven. Het boek is the thing given, and aan je broer identifies the recipient. Je before broer is possessive your. The recipient may also precede the object without aan: Geef je broer het boek.

Stuur het me op..explanation: Opsturen separates into imperative stuur and particle op. Het is the thing and me the recipient; both precede op. Naar me/mij can also identify the destination/recipient explicitly in the alternate models.

Kom morgen op tijd..explanation: Kom is the imperative of komen and leaves out the subject. Morgen means tomorrow. Op tijd means on time; op is part of that phrase here, not a particle of a separable verb opkomen.

Bel de tandarts terug..explanation: Terugbellen means call back and separates into imperative bel and particle terug. De tandarts is the person to call. The instruction concerns returning the call, not merely calling an unrelated person.

Doe de deur op slot..explanation: Doe is the imperative of doen. De deur is the object and op slot means locked. The whole expression de deur op slot doen means lock the door; op slot stays a separate phrase.

Laten we een nieuw restaurant proberen..explanation: Laten we introduces the shared suggestion and proberen stays an infinitive. Restaurant is a singular het-word, so indefinite een takes nieuw without -e. The group proposes eating there to try it.

Laten we de vergadering verzetten..explanation: Laten we makes a shared suggestion and verzetten remains an infinitive. Verzetten means reschedule this meeting; it does not specify an earlier or later time. Uitstellen would explicitly mean postpone.

Laten we het raam openmaken..explanation: After laten we, openmaken stays joined as an infinitive without te. Compare a direct imperative Maak het raam open, which separates maak and open. Het raam is the window the group proposes opening.

Laten we onze vakantie plannen..explanation: Laten we proposes the shared activity. Onze agrees with de vakantie, even though vakantie is singular. Plannen is the final infinitive; this suggests arranging the holiday rather than reporting that plans already exist.

Laten we het probleem bespreken..explanation: Laten we makes a shared suggestion and bespreken remains an infinitive. Bespreken takes the topic directly as object het probleem, without over. Compare praten over het probleem, which does require over.

Laten we morgen verdergaan..explanation: Laten we proposes a shared action. Verdergaan remains an infinitive without te and stays joined after laten; compare finite we gaan verder. Morgen places the proposed continuation tomorrow.

Hij is aan het koken..explanation: Hij takes singular is. Aan het koken marks cooking as ongoing; koken remains an infinitive. Hij kookt can describe the same current activity without an explicit progressive.

Ik ben de soep aan het maken..explanation: Ik takes ben. De soep is what the speaker is making and precedes aan het maken. Maken stays an infinitive; English uses making. This describes work in progress, not a finished soup.

Wij zijn Nederlands aan het leren..explanation: Plural wij takes zijn. Nederlands is the language being learned and comes before aan het leren. Leren stays an infinitive. Wij leren Nederlands can also describe the ongoing learning.

Zij is een boek aan het lezen..explanation: Singular is identifies zij as she here. Een boek is the object before aan het lezen. Lezen stays an infinitive; zij leest een boek can describe the same current reading.

Hij is de ramen aan het schoonmaken..explanation: Is agrees with hij, and de ramen is the object. Schoonmaken remains joined after aan het; de ramen schoon aan het maken is also standard. In the simple present it splits: hij maakt de ramen schoon.

Mijn manager is ons aan het bellen..explanation: Mijn manager is one person, so use is. Ons is the object, the group receiving the call, and precedes aan het bellen. Bellen stays an infinitive. Mijn manager belt ons describes the same ongoing call.

Ik was mijn kamer aan het opruimen..explanation: Was is past of zijn here, not the verb wassen. Mijn kamer is the object of opruimen, before aan het. This describes tidying in progress at a past moment and does not claim the room was finished.

Wij waren op de trein aan het wachten..explanation: Wij takes plural past waren. Wachten op means wait for, so op de trein names what the group awaited; it does not mean on board the train here. Aan het wachten is the ongoing activity.

Hij is zijn kleren aan het wassen..explanation: Hij takes is. Zijn before kleren means his, while wassen is the infinitive for washing. The object zijn kleren precedes aan het wassen. Hij wast zijn kleren is the corresponding simple present.

Zij was een verslag aan het schrijven..explanation: Zij means she here and takes singular past was. Een verslag is the report being written and comes before aan het schrijven. This past progressive does not establish that she completed the report.

We zijn de tafel aan het dekken..explanation: Plural we takes zijn. De tafel dekken means set the table for a meal; dekken is the infinitive in aan het dekken. The object de tafel precedes that progressive phrase. We dekken de tafel is also possible.

Hij is bezig met koken..explanation: Hij takes is. Bezig met introduces what occupies him; koken names the cooking activity. Both met koken and met het koken are possible. If an article is used for this nominalised infinitive, use het, not de.

Hij is bezig met de was..explanation: Hij takes is. De was is a noun meaning the laundry, not a finite form of wassen here. Bezig met describes being occupied with that laundry. It can include several laundry tasks without specifying a single washing action.

Zij is bezig met het schoonmaken van de.explanation: Zij means she and takes is. Het schoonmaken names the cleaning activity as a noun; van de ramen identifies what is cleaned. With a verbal te-clause instead say Zij is bezig de ramen schoon te maken, splitting schoonmaken around te.

Ik ben bezig met het schrijven van een b.explanation: Ik takes ben. Het schrijven is a nominalised infinitive after met; van een brief identifies what is being written. The verbal alternative puts that object before te schrijven: Ik ben bezig een brief te schrijven.

Wij zijn bezig met het plannen van onze.explanation: Wij takes plural zijn. Het plannen names the planning activity after met. Van onze vakantie identifies what is planned; vakantie is a de-word, so our is onze. This describes ongoing arrangements, not a completed booking.

Hij was bezig met het opruimen van zijn.explanation: Was is past of zijn and agrees with hij. Het opruimen names tidying after met, and van zijn kamer identifies the room. Zijn before kamer means his. Being busy tidying does not imply the task was completed.

Zij was bezig met koken..explanation: Singular was identifies zij as she here and places the activity in the past. Koken names the activity after bezig met; het koken is also possible. This says she was occupied with cooking, without claiming completion.

Ik ben met mijn huiswerk bezig..explanation: Ik takes ben. Met mijn huiswerk identifies what occupies the speaker and precedes bezig in this model. Ik ben bezig met mijn huiswerk is also possible. Huiswerk is a noun, not an infinitive; no te is needed.

Wij zijn bezig met het lezen van het ver.explanation: Plural wij takes zijn. Het lezen names the reading activity after met; van het verslag identifies the report. Verslag is a het-word. This describes reading in progress rather than having finished the report.

Hij is klaar met het lezen van het boek..explanation: Klaar met means finished with, unlike bezig met, which means busy with. Het lezen names the reading activity; van het boek identifies what was read. Klaar om te lezen would mean ready to start reading, a different situation.

Zij is verantwoordelijk voor het opruime.explanation: Singular is identifies zij as she. Verantwoordelijk voor means responsible for; het opruimen names the assigned tidying activity. Responsibility does not establish that she is tidying right now or has already finished.

Ik probeer te slapen..explanation: Ik takes present probeer. Proberen introduces te + infinitive: te slapen. The statement reports an effort to sleep, not success. Compare past ik probeerde and perfect ik heb geprobeerd.

Hij probeert Nederlands te leren..explanation: Hij takes probeert, with the ordinary present -t. Nederlands is the language and precedes te leren. Proberen requires te before this infinitive; the sentence describes an effort, not proven proficiency.

Wij probeerden de deur te openen..explanation: Wij takes plural past probeerden. De deur is the object of openen, before te openen. Proberen introduces the te-infinitive, and its past tense locates the attempt earlier without saying the door opened.

Ik zal proberen te bellen..explanation: Zal is finite and agrees with ik. Proberen remains a bare infinitive after zal, but proberen in turn requires te before bellen. This promises an attempt to call rather than guaranteeing a successful call.

Ik ben hier om je te helpen..explanation: Ben agrees with ik and hier gives the location. Om je te helpen is a purpose clause: je is the listener receiving help, before te helpen. Om does not identify the recipient; object je does.

Zij is klaar om te vertrekken..explanation: Zij means she and takes is. Klaar om te vertrekken describes readiness to leave, not a completed departure. Vertrekken is inseparable and remains an infinitive after te. Compare separable weg te gaan, which can express the same intended departure.

Het is belangrijk om op tijd te komen..explanation: Belangrijk evaluates the infinitive clause and has no agreement -e. Op tijd means on time and precedes te komen. Om may be omitted here, but te remains: Het is belangrijk op tijd te komen.

Ik heb tijd om het af te maken..explanation: Heb is present of hebben, meaning have time here rather than a perfect auxiliary. Het names the task. Afmaken is separable, so its te-infinitive is af te maken; om introduces the activity there is time for and can be omitted.

Wij zijn van plan om deel te nemen..explanation: Wij takes plural zijn. Van plan zijn means intend or plan; it does not report participation already completed. Deelnemen is separable: deel te nemen with te between deel and nemen. Om introduces the intended action.

Hij vraagt me om terug te bellen..explanation: Vraagt is singular present with hij. Me is the person asked and the understood caller in the infinitive clause. Terugbellen means call back and splits around te: terug te bellen. Om is optional in this request complement.

Ik heb zin om naar buiten te gaan..explanation: Zin hebben om expresses feeling like doing something. Heb is finite with ik. Naar buiten gives the direction and te gaan is the infinitive. This expresses inclination, not a claim that the speaker already went outside.

Het is moeilijk om dat uit te leggen..explanation: Moeilijk evaluates the explaining activity. Dat is the matter to explain, before uit te leggen. Uitleggen is separable, so te occurs between uit and leggen. Om may be omitted in this infinitive clause.

Hij maakt de ramen schoon..explanation: Schoonmaken means clean dirt away. Its finite present splits into maakt with singular hij and particle schoon after object de ramen. Compare infinitive schoonmaken and perfect heeft schoongemaakt. This scenario describes his usual task.

Wij bellen de klant terug..explanation: Terugbellen is separable: plural wij takes bellen and terug comes after de klant. The customer receives the return call. The present can describe the next intended action as well as a regular practice; no completed call is claimed here.

Zij heeft de keuken schoongemaakt..explanation: Singular heeft identifies zij as she here. Schoongemaakt is the participle of separable schoonmaken, with ge between schoon and maakt. De keuken is the object before the participle. The perfect reports the completed cleaning.

Wij nemen water mee..explanation: Meenemen means take along. Wij takes plural nemen; mee separates and follows object water. Water is normally a mass noun here without an article. The present describes the water your group takes on the outing.

Hij heeft een boek meegenomen..explanation: Hij takes heeft in this perfect. Meegenomen is the participle of meenemen: mee + genomen, with the irregular participle of nemen. Een boek is what he brought along, before the participle. This reports completed bringing.

Ik heb tijd om de kamer op te ruimen..explanation: Heb means have in the expression tijd hebben. Opruimen means tidy up, not necessarily wash away dirt. Its te-infinitive is op te ruimen; de kamer is its object. Om can be omitted in this infinitive complement.

Zij woonde de vergadering bij..explanation: Bijwonen means attend and is separable: woonde ... bij. Singular past woonde identifies zij as she. De vergadering is the event attended, a direct object without a preposition. This differs from wonen meaning reside and does not mean she organised the meeting.

We nemen deel aan de cursus..explanation: Deelnemen aan means participate in. Plural we takes nemen; deel separates and aan introduces the activity, de cursus. Compare infinitive deelnemen and te-infinitive deel te nemen. Deel is not the object meaning one share here.

Ik voel me vandaag goed..explanation: For how someone feels use zich voelen. Ik takes voel and reflexive me, which refers back to the speaker. Vandaag gives the time and goed describes the feeling. English normally omits myself in this meaning.

Hij voelt zich moe..explanation: Hij takes voelt and reflexive zich. Moe describes how he feels and has no agreement -e. The reflexive belongs to zich voelen in this sense; compare non-reflexive ik voel de stof, where someone feels a fabric.

Wij voelen ons welkom..explanation: Plural wij takes voelen, and ons is the reflexive referring to the same group. Welkom describes their feeling of being accepted and has no attributive ending. Natural English says We feel welcome without ourselves.

Zij maakte zich zorgen..explanation: Zich zorgen maken means worry. Singular past maakte identifies zij as she here; zich refers back to her. Zorgen is part of this idiom. This reports past worry, not making physical objects called worries.

Ik vraag me af waar hij is..explanation: Zich afvragen means wonder: ik vraag me af. Me refers to ik and af separates from finite vraag. Waar hij is is an embedded question, with is at its end. A direct question instead has Waar is hij?

Wij vragen ons af wanneer de trein komt..explanation: Wij takes plural vragen and reflexive ons. Af is the separable particle of afvragen. The embedded question wanneer de trein komt has finite komt after its subject. Present komt can refer to the anticipated arrival; no zullen is required.

Hij herinnert zich mijn naam..explanation: Zich herinneren means remember. Hij takes herinnert and reflexive zich; mijn naam is what he remembers. Mijn refers to the speaker, not the man. The unstressed prefix her- stays attached in this finite verb.

Ik herinner me die dag..explanation: Ik takes herinner and reflexive me in zich herinneren. Die modifies singular de-word dag and points to a day already mentioned. The remembering is present even though the remembered day is in the past.

Jullie haasten je..explanation: Jullie is the plural subject and takes haasten. Je is the reflexive referring back to that same group, not a singular subject or possessive here. Zich haasten means hurry; English needs no yourselves.

Zij stelt zich voor..explanation: Zich voorstellen means introduce oneself in this scenario. Singular stelt identifies zij as she, zich refers to her, and voor is the separable particle. The same Dutch expression can mean imagine in other contexts, so the introduction scenario determines the meaning.

Ik weet dat hij zich goed voelt..explanation: Weet is finite with ik in the main clause. Dat introduces the embedded statement hij zich goed voelt. Zich refers to hij, and finite voelt follows goed at the end of that clause. The speaker claims knowledge of his well-being.

Ik blijf thuis omdat ik ziek ben..explanation: Blijf is finite with ik in the main clause; thuis means at home. Omdat gives the reason and introduces ik ziek ben, with ben at the end. It is written as one word. The sentence explains staying home because of illness.

Ik weet dat hij morgen komt..explanation: Ik weet states knowledge. Dat introduces the embedded clause hij morgen komt, with finite komt at its end. Morgen makes the visit future even though komt has present form. English naturally uses is coming for the scheduled visit.

Als ik tijd heb, oefen ik Nederlands..explanation: Als introduces a condition, with heb at the end of ik tijd heb. That whole clause occupies first position, so finite oefen follows it before main-clause subject ik. Nederlands is the language practised. Compare Ik oefen Nederlands als ik tijd heb.

Toen ik thuiskwam, was ik moe..explanation: Toen introduces this past event; thuiskwam is past of thuiskomen and stays joined at the end of the subordinate clause. That whole clause comes first, so main-clause was precedes ik. Moe describes how the speaker felt when arriving home.

Hij leest terwijl ik kook..explanation: Leest agrees with hij in the main clause. Terwijl expresses the overlap and introduces ik kook; kook is finite with ik at the end of that clause. Both verbs have present form. English while connects the same simultaneous activities.

Ik bel je zodra ik thuis ben..explanation: Bel is present with ik but makes a promise about the next call here. Je is the listener receiving it. Zodra means as soon as and introduces ik thuis ben, with ben at the end. Thuis means at home; no future auxiliary is needed.
